nodes.label: Neo-Brutalist 'Void Dark' Theming
nodes.rationale: Pitch-black cards with offset borders and bright colour shadows; brand accent #06B8D4 cyan, void #0B0D12, text #F4F4F5, uppercase monospace.

nodes.label: 'Ink Depths' palette + 4-area app shell layout
nodes.rationale: CSS vars mirror src/app/globals.css (accent #53D8FF on void blacks) and the grid is topbar / tool-rail / stage / properties / pipeline strip so the mockup reads as the real editor.

nodes.label: Photoshop-parity View Modes
nodes.rationale: On Layers (checker), Overlay rubylith, On Black, On White, B&W matte and Marching Ants — mirrors Photoshop Select & Mask so the matte can be judged against different backdrops.

nodes.label: Megashader Mask Harness (standalone WebGL2 page)
nodes.rationale: Auth-free 3-column tile grid + log pane that runs the real megashader (radial/linear/pen-path masks, vibrance, texture, dehaze) from a prebuilt bundle.js, so shader work can be inspected without Next/Clerk.

nodes.label: Mask Lab — Select & Mask pipeline mockup (browser)
nodes.norm_label: mask lab — select & mask pipeline mockup (browser)
nodes.rationale: Single standalone HTML file, no build step and zero model downloads: the deep models are swapped for fast classical equivalents so the refine math you would actually ship can be evaluated offline.

nodes.label: Phosmith Mask Lab (Python CLI/Gradio tool)
nodes.rationale: A real (not stubbed) masking pipeline proven outside the editor first; it reuses the segment service venv so it needs no new installs except optional gradio.

nodes.label: Mask Lab deps reuse the segment service venv
nodes.norm_label: mask lab deps reuse the segment service venv
nodes.rationale: numpy/opencv/scipy/pymatting/rembg are already in ../../services/segment/.venv, so the documented run path is that interpreter; only gradio (optional, --ui) is extra.

nodes.label: Adjust Tool Parameter Set (15+ sliders)
nodes.rationale: Brightness/contrast/saturation/vibrance/exposure/temperature/tint/hue/highlights/shadows/sharpness/blur/noise/film grain/curves, all computed live in WebGL2.

nodes.label: Mask Tool Taxonomy (AI / Draw / Range / Destructive)
nodes.norm_label: mask tool taxonomy (ai / draw / range / destructive)
nodes.rationale: All non-destructive selections become reorderable, toggleable, invertible megashader mask layers; only Quick Erase modifies pixels.

nodes.label: Megashader WebGL2 Compositing Engine
nodes.rationale: Each mask layer stores parameters, not pixels, so it stays fully editable; the chain recompiles and re-renders at 60fps and is pinned by 230 GLSL invariant tests.

nodes.label: clerk-nextjs create-next-app Boilerplate README
nodes.rationale: Untouched create-next-app scaffold README (npm/yarn/pnpm instructions), unlike the main project which mandates Bun as the sole package manager — likely a leftover Clerk starter directory.

nodes.label: Scratch image-preview page (test.html)
nodes.rationale: Two bare tags at 800px pointing at absolute local paths inside a Gemini/Antigravity IDE artifact directory — a throwaway side-by-side viewer for captured bug frames, not part of the app.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0 Licensing Decision
nodes.rationale: Phosmith is a build input to Mask Studio, which bundles src/lib/megashader and the mask UI and is AGPL because of a YOLOE-derived detector; AGPL on Phosmith is what lets the two combine. AGPL section 13 means a hosted deployment must offer source, typically via a 'Source' link in the app shell.

nodes.label: autoSelect()
nodes.rationale: SAM stand-in: border-colour distance plus a centre prior, thresholded at 1.05x mean, then largest-component + hole-fill + tiny close.

nodes.label: fillHoles()
nodes.rationale: Flood-fills from the image border so only background reachable from outside stays background; everything enclosed becomes foreground.

nodes.label: Stage 1 — Coarse mask (rembg / GrabCut / saliency)
nodes.rationale: rembg wins on real photos (it is the model the FastAPI service ships); GrabCut wins when the subject is centred with clear contrast. Upgrade path is SAM 3.1 point/box/text, already wired as _load_sam3.

nodes.label: BiRefNet via rembg / ONNX Runtime
nodes.rationale: birefnet-general is the default; birefnet-general-lite (~215 MB) is the faster low-RAM option.

nodes.label: POST /segment (saliency subject matte)
nodes.rationale: Returns a PNG whose alpha channel is the subject matte, so the caller gets both cut-out and mask from one response.

nodes.label: rembg onnxruntime backend choice (cpu vs gpu)
nodes.norm_label: rembg onnxruntime backend choice (cpu vs gpu)
nodes.rationale: rembg needs an explicit backend: rembg[cpu] gives onnxruntime with the CoreML EP on Apple Silicon and works everywhere; rembg[gpu] is CUDA and Linux-only. Default is cpu for cross-platform installs.

nodes.label: AI Auto-Crop (4 strategies)
nodes.rationale: subject-aware, aspect-ratio, content-fill and depth-guided boxes are proposed and previewed in the existing crop overlay before the user commits.

nodes.label: POST /depth (normalized depth map)
nodes.rationale: Grayscale PNG with white = near and black = far, so it drops straight into a luminance-style mask layer.

nodes.label: GET /health probe
nodes.rationale: Reports status plus per-model availability flags, which is also what an uptime cron pings to keep a free Space awake.

nodes.label: Phosmith Mask Service (FastAPI, HF Space)
nodes.rationale: Docker-SDK Space bound to port 7860, Public so Vercel serverless routes can call it directly; Free CPU Basic 16 GB is stated as sufficient.

nodes.rationale: HF Spaces gives a free 16 GB CPU container; the Space must be Public so Vercel's backend can query it without OAuth. Free Spaces sleep after 48h and take 30-60s to wake, so ping /health on a cron to avoid timeouts. MASK_SERVICE_URL must have no trailing slash.

nodes.label: SEGMENT_EAGER_MODELS lazy loading default
nodes.rationale: Default 0 loads SAM and Depth on first request instead of at startup, keeping Space start times fast at the cost of a slow first call.

nodes.label: AI Object Remover (click -> SAM -> LaMa)
nodes.rationale: Professional-eraser behaviour: the object is segmented AND the hole is filled with plausible background, rather than cut to transparency. LaMa local-first with HF Stable Diffusion fallback, cropped to padded mask bounds.

nodes.label: Natural-Language Masking
nodes.rationale: mask.fromDescription chains CLIPSeg grounding + SAM refinement so each plan step lands as its own editable layer.

nodes.label: POST /sam2/click (positive/negative clicks)
nodes.rationale: Clicks are [x, y, label] tuples with 1 = include and 0 = exclude, returning a grayscale PNG mask.

nodes.label: Vercel Triangle Logomark
nodes.description: 1155x1000 single-path equilateral triangle filled #fff — the Vercel mark, drawn white so it only reads on dark surfaces (inverse constraint to next.svg).

nodes.label: Phosmith Badge Logo
nodes.description: 240x240 app-badge form of the brand: the same five-stream convergence mark placed on a dark rounded-rect (rx 28) with a radial-gradient field and dot grid, everything clipped to the badge. Heavily commented — the source doubles as the mark's construction spec.
nodes.rationale: Every luminosity is dialled DOWN versus logo-mark.svg (stream stops 0.72/0.78 not 0.85/0.9, halos 0.18 not 0.22, specular 0.86 not 0.9) because the dark field already supplies contrast; reusing the transparent version's values would bloom out.

nodes.label: Phosmith Logo Mark
nodes.description: 240x240 transparent-background brand mark: five glowing cubic-Bezier streams fanning right from a single cyan origin node, with luminous waypoint nodes and two violet pixel diamonds. role=img + aria-label/title 'Phosmith'. The backgroundless sibling of public/logo.svg.
nodes.rationale: Opacities run hotter than the badge version (0.85/0.9 stream stops, 0.22 halos vs 0.72/0.78 and 0.18) because it must hold up on unknown/light surfaces where the dark badge's contrast boost is absent.

nodes.label: Phosmith Favicon
nodes.description: 32x32 Next.js App Router file-convention icon: dark #0B0D12 rounded square (rx 7) carrying one cyan #06B8D4 four-point sparkle. Two elements total — no gradients, no filters, no clip.
nodes.rationale: Same dark-rounded-badge silhouette as logo.svg but the entire stream/node/glow system is discarded: at 16-32 CSS px hairline 1.2px strokes and stdDeviation-16 blurs turn to mud, so the identity is carried by silhouette + the single cyan token instead.

nodes.label: Next.js Wordmark
nodes.description: 394x80 black wordmark spelling NEXT with the trailing registered-mark/JS lockup as outlined glyph paths. Vendor framework branding, fill hardcoded #000 so it only reads on light surfaces.

nodes.label: create-next-app Default Asset Set
nodes.rationale: These five SVGs are the untouched create-next-app scaffold payload (file/globe/window UI glyphs + next/vercel vendor marks), shipped by the generator rather than authored for Phosmith. They live in the clerk-nextjs/ sub-app, are disjoint from the Phosmith brand system in public/ and src/app/, and carry vendor-fixed colors (#000 / #fff) that no product theme token controls.

nodes.label: Dark Radial Badge Field
nodes.rationale: Radial gradient #0F1622 -> #08090D with its centre pushed to cx 36% — offset to sit under the origin node at x=58/240 (24%) so the background is subtly brightest exactly where the light source is, faking a single-source lighting model rather than a flat plate.

nodes.label: Subtle Dot Grid Pattern
nodes.rationale: 18x18 userSpaceOnUse tile with one r=0.72 white dot at 6.5% opacity, painted as a second full-bleed rect over the gradient. Reads as engineering graph paper / a canvas transparency grid at full size and vanishes at favicon scale; deliberately below the threshold where it competes with the streams.

nodes.label: Cyan-Violet Brand Palette
nodes.rationale: Four literal tokens carry the whole identity: #06B8D4 cyan (primary/hero stream, origin core), #22D3EE bright cyan (highlight tail and far node), #7C3AED violet (outer arcs, secondary nodes), #8B5CF6 light violet (accent dots, pixel diamonds). Near-complementary cyan/violet on near-black; no colour is theme-driven, every value is inlined in each SVG.

nodes.label: Origin Convergence Node
nodes.rationale: The single point (58,120) where every stream converges, built as six stacked circles: two hairline concentric rings (r22/r14, opacity ~0.2) reading as orbit, two blurred cyan fills for bloom, a solid r4.5 cyan core, and an r2.4 white specular highlight. The white dot is what makes it read as a light source rather than a flat dot.

nodes.label: Pixel Diamond Node
nodes.rationale: A 4.5x4.5 rounded square rotated 45 degrees about its own centre, sitting on the top and bottom arcs. The only non-circular element in the mark — a literal PIXEL turned on its corner, the one motif that states 'photo software' rather than generic network-graph.

nodes.label: Five-Stream Bezier Fan
nodes.rationale: Five cubic Beziers all begin 'M 58,120' and fan top-right to bottom-right, mirrored about y=120 (streams 1/5 and 2/4 are reflections; stream 3 is the axis). Stroke weight encodes hierarchy — 2.8px cyan hero centre, 1.8px violet outer arcs, 1.2px accents — so the eye lands on the centre stream first. Depicts many signals refined into one processed output: the visual thesis of a photo-editing pipeline.

nodes.label: Four-Point Sparkle Glyph
nodes.rationale: One closed path of four concave quadratic-feel cubic arcs from (16,3)/(29,16)/(16,29)/(3,16) — a four-point star with pinched waists, the conventional 'AI / enhance' sparkle. Solid fill instead of a blur stack: it reads as emitted light at tiny sizes where an actual glow filter cannot.

nodes.label: Parametric Bezier Node Placement
nodes.rationale: Node coordinates are not eyeballed: each is derived by evaluating the parent stream's cubic B(t) at a chosen t (0.50 for arc midpoints, 0.72/0.76 for outboard nodes), with the Bernstein coefficients and the full arithmetic written out in the comment above every circle. Guarantees nodes sit exactly ON their stream and makes the mark reproducible/re-derivable after any control-point edit; mirrored streams reuse results by symmetry about y=120.

nodes.label: Rounded-Rect Glow Clip
nodes.rationale: A clipPath rect matching the badge (240x240, rx 28) wraps every stream, node and ambient halo. Source comment: 'Clip to rounded rect so glows stay contained'. Without it the oversized blur regions and the stream tails (which run to x=204 and beyond) would spill past the badge silhouette and break the icon's square footprint.

nodes.label: Two-Family Glow Filter Set
nodes.rationale: Two deliberately distinct filter families. fB3/fB6/fB10/fB16 are blur-ONLY (no feMerge) so they are applied to separate throwaway halo shapes stacked beneath a crisp sibling. fG3/fG5 feMerge the blur UNDER SourceGraphic so a single element keeps a sharp core while gaining bloom. Filter regions are hugely oversized (up to 900% / -400%) because default -10%/120% clips a stdDeviation-16 blur into a visible square edge.

nodes.label: userSpaceOnUse Stream Gradients
nodes.rationale: lg1-lg5 use gradientUnits=userSpaceOnUse with x1/y1 pinned to the origin (58,120) and x2/y2 to each stream's endpoint, so colour advances along the true path angle instead of the bounding box's diagonal. Every ramp starts at stop-opacity 0 and ends near 0.1 — the strokes dissolve into the origin bloom and fade out at their tails so no hard stroke-cap is ever visible. The outer/inner pairs invert hue direction (violet->cyan on lg2, cyan->violet on lg4) to bind the two colours together.

nodes.label: boxFilter()
nodes.rationale: Separable O(N) running-sum box filter, edge-normalised by valid-window count so borders do not darken.

nodes.label: buildMatte()
nodes.rationale: Re-imposes the trimap's hard FG/BG constraints after the guided filter so only the unknown band is actually solved.

nodes.label: gaussBlur()
nodes.rationale: Three box passes approximate a gaussian, avoiding a real kernel while staying O(N).

nodes.label: globalRefine()
nodes.rationale: Smooth / Shift Edge / Contrast / Feather applied in that fixed order — Photoshop Global Refinements parity.

nodes.label: guidedFilter()
nodes.rationale: He et al. guided filter on the luminance guide is the edge-aware matting core: it pulls soft alpha onto real luminance edges (hair, fur, fringe).

nodes.label: pymattingRefine()
nodes.rationale: Close-then-open on the solid core bridges pinholes and drops speckles, but soft edge pixels are left untouched so hair is not hardened.

nodes.label: recompute()
nodes.rationale: Coalesces non-immediate recomputes into one requestAnimationFrame so slider drags never queue multiple full-pipeline passes.

nodes.label: MAT_PRESET matting model presets (guided / vitmatte / zim)
nodes.norm_label: mat_preset matting model presets (guided / vitmatte / zim)
nodes.rationale: The 'deep model' choice is only a radius-factor/epsilon tuple on the guided filter — it emulates detail strength rather than pretending to run the real weights.

nodes.label: Refine Edge brush (forces trimap 'unknown')
nodes.rationale: Painting refine marks pixels unknown in the trimap regardless of their current FG/BG state, handing them to the matting solver to recover hair detail.

nodes.label: Smart Radius (gradient-widened trimap band)
nodes.rationale: A second, wider erode/dilate pair is used only where the smoothed luminance gradient exceeds 0.10, and the wide radius is capped at 34px to keep morphology interactive.

nodes.label: Mask Boundary Extension (Boundary slider)
nodes.rationale: Grows/shrinks by an absolute px amount from the pristine texture kept under baseTextureKey, so setting 0 always restores the original edge (non-cumulative).

nodes.label: WORK_MAX working-resolution cap (760px)
nodes.rationale: All CPU pipeline math runs at a downscaled working resolution so the full coarse->trimap->matte->refine chain stays interactive on every slider move.

nodes.label: decontaminate()
nodes.rationale: Iteratively floods known-foreground colour inward (max 22 passes) to unmix background colour out of partially transparent pixels.

nodes.label: Production mapping modal (mockup stage -> real model)
nodes.norm_label: production mapping modal (mockup stage -> real model)
nodes.rationale: Each stage is tagged sim or real in the UI and the modal states the exact production wiring: SAM 3.1 via /api/ai/sam2 + /api/ai/ground, a new lazy-loaded /matte endpoint for ZIM/ViTMatte, PyMatting behind a quality toggle, and a final maskTextureKey on a megashader chain layer.

nodes.label: Stage 5 — Decontaminate (PyMatting estimate_foreground_ml)
nodes.rationale: Foreground colour estimation unmixes background bleed out of semi-transparent edge pixels; skippable with --no-decon.

nodes.label: Stage 3 — Fine matte (PyMatting closed-form / KNN)
nodes.rationale: Closed-form matting is where quality is won on hair/fur; when ZIM or ViTMatte is dropped in, PyMatting demotes to a polish pass rather than being removed.

nodes.label: Coarse -> Trimap -> Matte -> Refine -> Decontaminate pipeline
nodes.norm_label: coarse -> trimap -> matte -> refine -> decontaminate pipeline
nodes.rationale: Only the coarse segmenter stands in for SAM 3.1; every later stage is production math, so the fine-matte stage recovers hair/fur regardless of which coarse engine was used.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — Trimap (OpenCV erode/dilate band)
nodes.rationale: Identical to Matte-Anything's generate_trimap and marked 'unchanged' on the upgrade path; wider band recovers more hair at the cost of speed.

nodes.label: ZIM (zim_vit_l) drop-in matting upgrade
nodes.rationale: Replacing fine_matte() with a ZimPredictor call keeps the surrounding trimap/refine/decontaminate stages untouched — the pipeline was shaped so each stage is swappable.

nodes.label: SAM3_REFINE_MATTING alpha-matting refinement
nodes.rationale: PyMatting closed-form is the quality path for hair-level edges; the cv2 guided-filter fallback needs only opencv, so the feature degrades instead of requiring pymatting.

nodes.label: Agent Command Registry
nodes.rationale: Every editor capability is a named command so agent chat, verify scripts and keyboard shortcuts all drive the same code path; refcounted beginAgentAction/endAgentAction gives free agent attribution in the change journal.

nodes.label: Collage Engine (pure geometry)
nodes.rationale: Geometry kept React-free so tool UI and agent commands share it; cells use Fabric absolutePositioned clipPaths and Shadow objects so the layout serializes natively with canvas state and cellFromClipPath can recover bounds on reload.

nodes.label: Neon/Postgres + Prisma Backend
nodes.rationale: Prisma models are the source of truth for users, projects, canvas state, revisions, AI caches and telemetry; never bypass the lazy helpers in src/lib/prisma.js.

nodes.label: Agent Command System (mask./crop./collage. domains)
nodes.rationale: Domains are registered by canvas.jsx on editor mount and exposed as window.__phosmith.agent; every run is logged in the History panel with a cyan Bot badge, separate from user changes.

nodes.label: AI Agent (Agentic Editing) prompt routing
nodes.rationale: Prompts route to collage (COLLAGE_INTENT_RE), edit (Gemini grade loop: executor -> judge -> critic -> corrective re-plan, max 3 iterations) or mask (NL -> CLIPSeg + SAM) paths.

nodes.label: AI Caching & Deterministic Planning
nodes.rationale: Identical requests keyed by dHash perceptual hash + prompt are cached in Postgres; Gemini runs at fixed seed 42 with a structured responseSchema so a cache hit is a correct answer. JUDGE_VERSION / PLANNER_VERSION must be bumped to invalidate.

nodes.label: Canvas State Write-Behind Caching
nodes.rationale: Updates batch/debounce in Redis and flush async to Postgres; visibilitychange->hidden uses a normal flush (not beaconUnload) so baseRevision advances and no spurious 'edited on another device' conflict appears.

nodes.label: Undo/Redo Object Identity Rule
nodes.rationale: loadFromJSON rebuilds every Fabric object, so references go stale — match by src/props, never identity. Never commit a blob: URL: it is page-scoped and revokes on navigation, breaking persistence and undo; upload to ImageKit with a data:-URL fallback.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrations over db:push
nodes.rationale: db:push is the dev path; a production-controlled rollout uses prisma:migrate instead.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL vs DIRECT_URL
nodes.rationale: The app runs on the pooled Neon connection string; Prisma schema operations need the direct string, so both are configured separately.

nodes.label: Redis Cache Durability Requirement
nodes.rationale: Without Upstash/Redis vars the temporary cache is in-memory: fine for development, but not durable and unable to coordinate between multiple server instances.

nodes.label: Per-Capability AI Routing Policy
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for where each capability runs; resolveOrder() returns preferred-side-first with the other side as runtime fallback so a missing side degrades instead of failing.

nodes.label: In-Browser AI Engines (transformers.js)
nodes.rationale: WebGPU->WASM device fallback, golden-input calibration gate and sticky engine demotion make the client path verifiable rather than works-on-my-machine.

nodes.label: Local FastAPI AI Selection Service
nodes.rationale: Heavy CV inference is offloaded to a local Python process so it never blocks the Node.js thread; reached via MASK_SERVICE_URL.

nodes.label: Megashader Masking Engine
nodes.rationale: One WebGL2 fragment shader evaluates the whole chain of 7 mask kinds plus boolean composition, so any number of layers costs one GPU pass instead of N compositing passes.

nodes.label: cleanSubjectMatte (on-device matte cleanup under test)
nodes.rationale: Turns a soft RMBG-1.4 matte into a solid hole-free selection; it is the fallback path, since the SAM 3.1 mask service is preferred whenever reachable.

nodes.label: mask-verify — subject-mask cleanup regression test
nodes.rationale: T1-T4 guard hole fill, speck removal, keeping a second smaller figure, backlit luminance assist, and resolution-independence of holesFilledFrac above the 1536px downscale cap.

nodes.label: Brush Latency: contextTop compositing
nodes.rationale: requestRenderAll mid-stroke forces a full scene redraw plus an after:render DOM sync every frame, causing cursor lag; in-stroke feedback therefore goes on Fabric's contextTop, and getCoalescedEvents() keeps high-Hz mice smooth.

nodes.label: RMBG-1.4 Manual Recipe (client matting)
nodes.rationale: AutoModel with model_type:'custom' plus an explicit processor config is the only matting engine that works in this onnxruntime-web build; BiRefNet-lite / MODNet via pipeline() fail, so do not 'simplify' back to them.

nodes.label: _canvas-shim.mjs pure-JS canvas
nodes.rationale: Unlike the other verify scripts this code delegates to canvas ops, and node-canvas needs system cairo/pango that are not built here. The cleanup path uses canvas only as a pixel buffer (no path/text rasterisation), so an ImageData-backed shim is exact — but drawImage must implement real source-over, because fillEnclosedMaskRegions depends on transparent source pixels leaving the destination unchanged.

nodes.label: Scoped tsconfig @/ alias + megashader stub
nodes.rationale: The app resolves @/ through next.config.mjs's webpack alias, which bun cannot read, and there is no root tsconfig. A tsconfig scoped to this subdir maps @/* -> src/* without affecting next build, and @/lib/megashader resolves to a stub because growMaskCanvas imports four names from that barrel at load time but never calls them in the cleanup path.

nodes.label: Local AI Services Setup & Verification
nodes.rationale: Without the service SAM/Depth/YOLO/CLIPSeg/LaMa return 501 and Select Subject falls back to HuggingFace; the editor is designed to stay usable degraded.

nodes.label: numpy<2 pin chain for sam3
nodes.rationale: sam3 requires numpy<2, so rembg is capped below 2.0.70 and opencv below 4.11 — raising either floor transitively pulls numpy 2.x and breaks the sam3 import.

nodes.label: SAM 3.1 gated install (not on PyPI)
nodes.rationale: Meta's package installs from GitHub and the facebook/sam3.1 checkpoint needs an accepted licence plus hf login; without it every SAM-3 route degrades to the saliency/None fallback rather than erroring.

nodes.label: sam3's undeclared runtime deps (einops, pycocotools, opencv)
nodes.norm_label: sam3's undeclared runtime deps (einops, pycocotools, opencv)
nodes.rationale: sam3.sam.rope imports einops and sam3.train.data needs pycocotools, but neither is declared in package metadata, so both are pinned here explicitly.

nodes.label: CPU triton stub (_ensure_triton_stub)
nodes.rationale: sam3 hard-imports NVIDIA triton, which has no macOS/Apple-Silicon wheel. main.py installs a CPU stub so the import succeeds; sam3.perflib already dispatches NMS / connected components to numpy/skimage off-GPU. On a CUDA host the real triton is used and the stub is a no-op.

nodes.label: Model size/quality trade-off notes
nodes.rationale: SAM Hiera variants run tiny 160 MB / small 180 MB / base-plus 340 MB / large 1.5 GB; Depth Anything V2 Small is ~100 MB vs Base 340 MB and Large 1.3 GB; LaMa is ~200 MB and MIT-licensed and reuses torch.

nodes.label: Optional deps degrade endpoints to 501
nodes.rationale: torch/transformers (SAM), Depth and simple-lama-inpainting are each optional: when absent the owning endpoint returns 501 while /segment keeps working, and the Next.js route falls back to HuggingFace SD inpainting.

nodes.label: Shared global Python env (no venv) forces version ceilings
nodes.norm_label: shared global python env (no venv) forces version ceilings
nodes.rationale: Because both services share one global environment rather than per-service venvs, rembg is capped below 2.0.70 and opencv below 4.11 to keep numpy<2 for sam3.
